MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:4:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:5:# Replacing one factor of a measurement-weighted overlap
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:7:The scalar estimates used to combine the two Pauli bases compare averaged
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:8:overlaps whose left factor is one complete measurement and whose right factors
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:9:are operator families at small state-dependent distance.  This module records
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:10:the corresponding Cauchy--Schwarz estimate.  The right-hand families are
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:11:arbitrary, so the estimate covers an ordered product of point effects, which
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:12:is not itself a measurement.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:13:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:14:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:15:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:16:The estimate is `lem:overlap-gap-distance` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:17:`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`; it is the Cauchy--Schwarz
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:18:step at paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:19:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1147-1166`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:20:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:29:/-- Replacing one operator family inside an overlap weighted on the left by a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:30:complete measurement changes the average by at most the square root of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:31:state-dependent squared distance between the two families. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:144:/-! ## The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality weighted by a positive operator -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:146:/-- For a positive operator `A`, the sesquilinear form `⟨u, A v⟩` satisfies the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:147:Cauchy--Schwarz inequality with the two diagonal values `⟨u, A u⟩` and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:148:`⟨v, A v⟩`.  This is the inequality behind the Cauchy--Schwarz steps of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:149:proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`, in which both factors carry
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:150:the square root of the line effect, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:151:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1209`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:186:/-- The sum over outcomes of the real parts of `⟨u a, A a (v a)⟩`, for
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:187:positive weights `A a`, is bounded by the product of the square roots of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:188:two diagonal sums. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:217:/-- The averaged form of the preceding estimate: the average over a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:218:distribution of the outcome sums of `Re ⟨u, A v⟩` is bounded by the product of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:219:the square roots of the two averaged diagonal sums. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:269:/-! ## Quadratic forms against projections -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:271:/-- The real quadratic form is invariant under the conjugate transpose. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:281:/-- Conjugating an operator transfers the outer operator to the state vector. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:292:/-- For a projection `B` commuting with `A`, the quadratic form of `A` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:293:`B ψ` is the quadratic form of `A B` in `ψ`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:301:/-- The quadratic form of an operator bounded by the identity is bounded by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:302:the squared norm of the vector. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:309:/-- The effects of a complete measurement have total quadratic form one on a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:310:unit vector. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:322:/-- Weighting a complete measurement by commuting projections cannot exceed
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:323:the total mass one. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:351:/-! ## Replacing a factor under the weight of a measurement -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:353:/-- Cauchy--Schwarz with the measurement as weight: for projections `B`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:354:commuting with the effects of `A`, the averaged overlap of `A` against the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:355:product `B C` is bounded by the square roots of the averaged overlap of `A`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:356:against `B` and of the averaged quadratic form of `A` in `C ψ`.  This is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:357:Cauchy--Schwarz step of the proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:358:paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1209`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:401:/-- Deficit form of the Cauchy--Schwarz estimate: for projections `B` and `C`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:402:commuting with the effects of `A`, replacing the factor `C B` by `C` inside an
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:403:overlap weighted by the complete measurement `A` changes the average by at
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:404:most the square root of the deficit `1 - E Σ_a ⟨A_a B_a⟩`.  This is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:405:estimate used in the proof of `lem:claim-17-2` and, with `C = Id`, in the proof
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:406:of `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:407:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1209`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:456:/-- The deficit form of the Cauchy--Schwarz estimate with the product family
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:457:`C B` supplied as one family `CB`, which is convenient when the product is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:458:formed on a local space before being placed. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:473:/-- Inserting an arbitrary operator family `W` after a projection family `R`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:474:commuting with the effects of `A` costs at most the square root of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:475:averaged squared norms of `W ψ`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:503:/-- The mirror image of the preceding estimate: an operator family `W`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:504:commuting with the effects of `A`, inserted before a commuting projection
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:505:family `R`, costs at most the square root of the averaged squared norms of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:506:`Wᴴ ψ`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean:3:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean:4:# Placement calculus on the expanded state
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean:5:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean:6:This module records the algebra of the four register placements used by the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean:7:combining argument: a placement is a unital `*`-homomorphism, placements on
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean:8:opposite register pairs commute, and the crosswise exchange of the two EPR
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean:9:pairs of the expanded state carries the placement `AA'` to `AB''` and `BA''`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean:10:to `BB'` while fixing the expanded state.  The last fact transfers every
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean:11:state-dependent distance between the two bipartition schemes of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean:12:`def:symmetric-equivalents` without assuming a symmetric strategy.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean:39:/-! ## Placements as reindexed tensor factors -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean:145:/-- A placement commutes with the conjugate transpose. -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:4:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:5:# Sub-line averages of the Z-point overlap
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7:The Z-point overlap of the paired-line measurement depends on the two source
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:8:lines and the Z block of the sampled extended point. The separate projected-point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:9:mixture properties of the directly indexed sub-line law identify each one-point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:10:marginal as a mixture of restricted product laws. Both marginal averaging
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:11:identities are recorded here. Regrouping line answers by their evaluations
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:12:then transfers the Z-overlap deficit from
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:13:`MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.ZEvalDeficit` to this law.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:14:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:15:The Z-overlap estimates hold for arbitrary opposite placements, with separate
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:16:first-player specializations. The concrete X-overlap deficit instead uses the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:17:exact X marginal of the X-Z-X sandwich and is proved in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:18:`MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.ConcreteXDeficit`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:19:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:20:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:21:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:22:The Z estimates support blueprint `lem:claim-17-3-re-direct`, alongside the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:23:source `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:24:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:25:The separate marginal identities encode the analogue of Property 2 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:26:`lem:qld-sublines` for the directly indexed law; source-distribution transport
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:27:remains separate.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:28:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:38:/-! ## Regrouping the line answers by their evaluations -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:40:/-- Summing a paired-line answer against a family of point effects that
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:41:depends on the answer only through its two evaluations is summing the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:42:evaluation classes of the paired-line measurement against that family.  This
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:43:is the fiber regrouping of the proofs of `lem:claim-17-1`, `lem:claim-17-2`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:44:and `lem:claim-17-3`, blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:45:`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2651-2830`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:132:/-- The sub-line average of a function of the two source lines and the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:133:`X`-point of the sampled extended point is a mixture of averages over products
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:134:of two restricted line-point laws, the `X`-point being the point of the first
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:135:factor. This is the use of Property~2 of `lem:qld-sublines` in the proof of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:136:`lem:claim-17-2`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:137:paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1201`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:166:/-- The sub-line average of a function of the two source lines and the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:167:`Z`-point of the sampled extended point is a mixture of averages over products
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:168:of two restricted line-point laws, the `Z`-point being the point of the second
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:169:factor.  This is the use of Property~2 of `lem:qld-sublines` in the proof of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:170:`lem:claim-17-3`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:171:paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:200:/-! ## The two one-point overlaps -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:207:/-- The overlap of the paired-line measurement at two source lines with the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:208:expanded `Z`-point effect at a point, summed over the line answers.  This is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:209:the integrand of the left-hand side of `lem:claim-17-3`, as a function of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:210:two source lines and the `Z`-point alone. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:219:/-- The original first-player specialization of the placed overlap. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:227:/-- At a pair of line-point pairs, the `Z`-point overlap is the overlap of the

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:266:/-- The original first-player specialization of the placed estimate. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:273:/-- The sub-line average of the `Z`-point overlap is at most one. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:312:/-- The original first-player specialization of the placed estimate. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:321:/-- The deficit of the sub-line average of the `Z`-point overlap is bounded by

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:323:deficit in the proof of `lem:claim-17-3`, blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:324:`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:325:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`. -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:7:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:8:# A uniform point of the extended space from the sub-line law
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:9:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:10:The first scalar estimate in the combining argument samples an extended line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:11:from the sub-line witness and then a uniform affine parameter on that line.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:12:This module records that the resulting extended point is uniform and hence
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:13:that its two source coordinate blocks are independent uniform points.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:14:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:15:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:16:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:17:These statements support `lem:claim-17-1` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:18:`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`.  The paper uses this sampling
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:19:fact at
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:20:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1159-1166`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:21:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:31:/-- If every slice of a map of a pair carries the second uniform law to one
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:32:fixed law, then the map carries the uniform law of the pair to that law. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:44:/-- Reading a point at a uniform affine parameter on the canonical line of a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:45:uniform direct sample gives a uniform point of the direct coordinate space. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:77:/-- Averaging a function at a uniform affine parameter on the canonical line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:78:of a uniform direct sample is averaging it at a uniform point. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:101:/-- A uniform point on a line drawn from the directly indexed line-point law
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:102:is uniform in the ambient coordinate space. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:130:/-- Identify the directly indexed extended coordinates with the combining
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:131:coordinate split. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:136:/-- Split an extended point into its two source blocks and two remaining
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:137:scalar coordinates. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:150:/-- The two source blocks of a uniform extended point are independent and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:151:uniform after the canonical scalar identification. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:165:/-- Under a sub-line witness, the two source blocks of the point at a uniform
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/UniformLinePoint.lean:166:affine parameter are independent uniform source points. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:6:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7:# Z-point deficits of the evaluated pair-line measurement
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:8:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:9:This module bounds the deficit of the overlap between the evaluated paired-line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:10:measurement and the expanded Z-point measurement. The proof inserts the completed
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:11:joint point measurement, replaces it by the X-then-Z ordered product, and sums
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:12:the X effects. It uses evaluated consistency and the distance from the joint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:13:point measurement to that ordered product. The bound holds first over any
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:14:probability law on pairs of line-point pairs and then over a product of restricted
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:15:line-point laws, whose point marginal is the uniform pair.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:16:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:17:The estimates hold for arbitrary opposite placements, with first-player
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:18:specializations; register commutation requires no symmetry of the state.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:19:The completed-outcome and real-overlap lemmas are also available for other
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:20:calculations. The concrete X-deficit argument is separate, in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:21:`MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.ConcreteXDeficit`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:22:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:23:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:24:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:25:The Z deficit supports blueprint `lem:claim-17-3-re-direct`, alongside the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:26:source `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:27:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`; the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:28:consistency input is `lem:qld-xz-lines` and the ordered products are those of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:29:`lem:qld-4-10`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:30:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:41:/-! ## Completed point pairs -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:43:/-- A sum over completed outcome pairs of a function vanishing on both `none`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:44:classes is the sum over the uncompleted pairs. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:63:/-- The completed joint measurement has the joint effect on a pair of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:64:evaluations. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:76:/-- The completed joint measurement vanishes on outcomes outside the image of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:77:the completion. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:87:/-- The completion of a projective joint measurement is projective. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:105:/-- A placed projection is a projection. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:115:/-- Every effect of the completed expanded point measurement is a projection,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:116:the `none` effect being zero. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:129:/-- The completed joint point measurement and a completed point product differ
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:130:only on outcome pairs with two evaluations, so their placed state-dependent
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:131:squared distance is the one of the joint point measurement and the point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:132:product.  Blueprint `ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2651-2698`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:160:/-- The completed `Z`-then-`X` point product vanishes on both `none` classes
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:161:and restricts to the ordered product on evaluated pairs. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:191:/-! ## The abstract one-point deficit -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:193:/-- Let `A` be a complete measurement, `Q` a projective measurement, `R` a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:194:family of projections and `W` a family of operators, all indexed by the same
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:195:outcomes, with `Q`, `R` and `W` commuting with the effects of `A` and with
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:196:`W R = W`.  If `A` and `Q` are consistent with defect at most `η` and `Q` is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:197:within squared distance `ζ` of `Wᴴ`, then the deficit of the overlap of `A`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:198:with `R` is at most `2 √η + 2 √ζ`.  The proof inserts `Q` before `R`, replaces
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:199:`Q R` by `W R = W`, and compares `W` with `Q`; each of the three steps is a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:200:Cauchy--Schwarz estimate weighted by `A`.  This is the common estimate behind
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:201:the deficits in the proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:202:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1239`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:235:  -- comparing `Q` with `W` under the weight `A`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:251:  -- replacing `Q R` by `W R = W`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:276:  -- inserting `Q` before `R`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:322:/-! ## The two placed deficits -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:324:/-- A pair of line-point pairs of the source space: the sample type of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:325:consistency display of `lem:qld-xz-lines`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:335:/-- The `Z`-point deficit of the evaluated pair-line measurement over a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:336:probability law on pairs of line-point pairs, from the consistency of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:337:evaluated pair-line measurement with the completed joint point measurement
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:338:and the closeness of the latter to the `Z`-then-`X` product.  This is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:339:deficit bounded in the proof of `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:340:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:451:/-- The original first-player specialization of the opposite-placement estimate. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:484:/-! ## The two deficits over a product of restricted line-point laws -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:486:/-- Every restricted line-point law has total mass one. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:496:/-- The point marginal of a restricted line-point law is uniform. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:505:/-- The pair of points of a product of two restricted line-point laws is a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:506:uniform pair. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:522:/-- A state-dependent distance between two families depending on the pair of

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:4:# Evaluation of line polynomials at a sampled point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:5:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:6:This module records the elementary calculus of the partial evaluation
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:7:`evalOpt` of a coefficient-list line polynomial at a point: the evaluation of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:8:a sum is the sum of the evaluations whenever both summands evaluate, a summand
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9:of an evaluating sum evaluates whenever the other summand does, the value is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:10:unique, and nothing evaluates at a point off the line. These facts underlie
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:11:the manipulation of the evaluation classes in items 2 and 3 of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:12:expanded-line consistency lemma.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:13:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:14:Every declaration below is a formalization-only auxiliary: the source uses
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:15:these facts about evaluation without stating them.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:16:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:17:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:18:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:19:The evaluation classes `[eval_u(·) = a]` are `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:20:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-58`. They are
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:21:manipulated in `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons` and `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:22:paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:23:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:31:/-- Coefficient-list evaluation is additive in the coefficient list. This
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:32:is the additivity behind the convolution of `def:expanded-line-measurement`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:40:/-- A line polynomial has at most one value at a point of the line: if it
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:41:evaluates both to `a` and to `b`, then `a = b`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:48:/-- The sum of two evaluating line polynomials evaluates to the sum of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:49:their values. This is why the convolution outcome `f = f' + f''` evaluates
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:50:whenever both convolution factors do. -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:5:# Overlap of expanded line and expanded point measurements
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:6:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:7:This module computes the diagonal overlap, on the expanded state, between an
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:8:expanded line measurement on one placement and the expanded point effects
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:9:selected by evaluation at the sampled point on the opposite placement. Each
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10:product of convolution terms factorizes into a strategy overlap and an EPR
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:11:overlap; the EPR overlap of a Pauli line projector with a Pauli point projector
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:12:vanishes unless the line polynomial evaluates to the point value, and then
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:13:equals the EPR overlap of the line projector alone. Summing over the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:14:convolution fibers identifies the expanded overlap with the overlap of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:15:strategy's evaluation classes and its completed point measurement. This is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:16:computation displayed in items 2 and 3 of the expanded-line consistency lemma.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:17:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:18:The sections on the linearity of the state quadratic form, on register
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:19:placements, and on the completed point measurements collect formalization-only
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:20:auxiliaries: the source uses these facts without stating them.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:242:/-- The diagonal quadratic form for the `AA'`--`BA''` product with distinct
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:243:Pauli factors factors into the strategy overlap and the first EPR-pair
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:244:overlap. This is the factorization behind the ancillary consistency in items
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:245:2 and 3 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:246:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:271:/-- The diagonal quadratic form for the `AB''`--`BB'` product with distinct
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:272:Pauli factors factors into the strategy overlap and the second EPR-pair
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:273:overlap, the Pauli factor of `BB'` acting on the first half of the pair.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:274:Paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:300:/-- Operators placed on `AA'` and on `BA''` commute. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:317:/-- Operators placed on `AB''` and on `BB'` commute. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:335:/-! ## The overlap identity -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:337:/-- The convolution-fiber rearrangement behind `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:338:and `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2`, at a point of the line. The statement is an
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:339:abstract bilinear identity: `Φ` and `Ψ` are any two functions of a pair of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:340:operators subject to the vanishing, additivity and factorization hypotheses
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:341:below, and the conclusion sums `Φ` over the convolution fibers of the expanded
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:342:line and point effects. It is applied with `Φ` the expanded overlap of two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:343:product operators on opposite placements and `Ψ` the strategy overlap, the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:344:factorization hypothesis then being the exact agreement of the ancillary
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:345:projectors `tau^{W,line}_{f''}` and `tau^{W,u}_{f''(u)}` on the EPR pairs; the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:346:conclusion is the overlap of the strategy's evaluation classes with its
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:347:completed point measurement. Paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:348:blueprint `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons`, `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:505:/-- Off the line, both sides of the overlap identity vanish: no line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:506:polynomial evaluates, so the selected point effects are zero and the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:507:evaluation classes with a proper value are empty. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:559:/-! ## The four placement pairs -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:561:/-- A strategy line effect is Hermitian, being positive semidefinite. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:568:/-- A strategy point effect is Hermitian, being positive semidefinite. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:575:/-- A Pauli line projector is Hermitian, being positive semidefinite. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:581:/-- A Pauli point projector is Hermitian, being positive semidefinite. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:588:/-- The expanded overlap of Alice's line measurement on `AA'` with Bob's
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:589:selected point effects on `BA''` is the strategy overlap of Alice's

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:592:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:593:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:560-596`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:674:/-- The expanded overlap of Bob's line measurement on `BA''` with Alice's
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:675:selected point effects on `AA'` is the strategy overlap of Alice's completed
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:676:point measurement with Bob's evaluation classes. This is the interchanged
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:677:form of the computation in items 2 and 3 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:678:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:560-596`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:762:/-- The expanded overlap of Alice's line measurement on `AB''` with Bob's
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:763:selected point effects on `BB'`, on the second bipartition. Paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:764:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:560-596`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:845:/-- The expanded overlap of Bob's line measurement on `BB'` with Alice's
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:846:selected point effects on `AB''`, on the second bipartition. Paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:847:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:560-596`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:4:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:5:# Pauli-register line projectors
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:6:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:7:This module constructs the projective measurement `tau^{W,line}` of one
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:8:generalized-Pauli register whose outcome is the restriction to a canonical
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:9:line of the low-degree encoding of the measured basis label. It records that
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:10:the outcome projectors are orthogonal projections summing to the identity,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11:that they are symmetric matrices (so that they act identically on either half
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:12:of an EPR pair), and that on an axis-parallel line they vanish outside the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:13:embedded degree-`d` subspace.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:14:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:15:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:16:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:17:The projectors are `tau^{W,line}_{f''}` of `def:expanded-line-measurement`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:18:with paper source
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:19:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. Their
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:20:perfect self-consistency on an EPR pair is the ancillary input to item 1 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:21:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:22:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:23:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:34:/-- The Pauli-register projector onto labels whose low-degree encoding
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:35:restricts to `f` on `line`. This is `tau^{W,line}_f` in the proof of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:36:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:37:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`, blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:38:`def:expanded-line-measurement`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:46:/-- Pauli line projectors are positive semidefinite. This is the positivity of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:47:the ancillary measurement in `def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:48:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:56:/-- The line coarse-graining of the generalized Pauli projectors is a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:57:symmetric matrix. Symmetry is what makes the projector act identically on
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:58:either half of an EPR pair, and hence is the hypothesis behind the perfect
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:59:ancilla consistency used in `enu:qld-comm-line-self-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:60:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:67:/-- Pauli line projectors belonging to distinct line polynomials are
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:68:orthogonal, while each projector is idempotent. This is the ancillary product
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:69:calculation in `def:expanded-line-measurement` and item 1 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:70:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:71:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-558`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:100:/-- The line fibers partition the complete family of Pauli eigenspace
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:101:projectors. This is the completeness of the ancillary measurement in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:102:`def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:103:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:117:/-- The projective line measurement on one Pauli register obtained by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:118:measuring the generalized Pauli basis and restricting the low-degree encoding
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:119:of the outcome to `line`. This is the ancillary measurement of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:120:`def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:121:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:128:/-- The effects of the Pauli line measurement are the line projectors. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:133:/-- On an axis-parallel line, Pauli line projectors vanish outside the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:134:embedded degree-`d` subspace, because every restricted low-degree encoding has
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:135:degree at most `d` there. This is the ancillary half of the last assertion of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:136:`def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:137:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:152:/-! ## Interaction with the point projectors -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:154:/-- On a point of the line, Pauli line projectors of non-evaluating
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:155:polynomials vanish: every restricted low-degree encoding evaluates there.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:156:Formalization-only auxiliary for items 2 and 3 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:157:paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:174:/-- A Pauli line projector followed by a Pauli point projector at a point of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:175:the line is the line projector when the line polynomial evaluates to the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:176:point value, and zero otherwise. This is the exact consistency
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:177:`tau^{W,line}_{f''}` versus `tau^{W,u}_{f''(u)}` in items 2 and 3 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:178:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:179:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:216:/-- Pauli line and point projectors commute. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:232:/-- Acting with a Pauli line projector on one half of the EPR state and a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:233:Pauli point projector on the other half equals acting with their product on
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:234:the first half. Formalization-only support for the exact ancillary
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:235:consistency in items 2 and 3 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:236:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:255:/-- On an EPR pair, a point projector on the first factor and a line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:256:projector on the second act as the product of the two projectors on the first
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:257:factor alone. This is the transport with the two factors interchanged, and it
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:258:uses the symmetry of the line projector rather than that of the point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:259:projector. Formalization-only auxiliary for the ancillary consistency of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:260:`def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:261:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:280:/-- The EPR quadratic form of a line projector on one half and a point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:281:projector on the other half is the EPR quadratic form of the line projector
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:282:alone when the line polynomial evaluates to the point value, and zero
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:283:otherwise. This is the exact ancillary consistency in items 2 and 3 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:284:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:285:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:313:/-- The EPR overlap of a point projector on the first factor with a line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:314:projector on the second vanishes unless the line polynomial evaluates at the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:315:point to the measured value, and otherwise equals the overlap of the line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:316:projector alone. This is the interchanged form of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:317:`stateQForm_eprState_tauLineProj_tauPointProj`, supporting
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:318:`def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:319:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:347:/-! ## Perfect consistency on an EPR pair -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:349:/-- Acting with the same Pauli line projector on both halves of the EPR state
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:350:equals acting on one half. Symmetry transports the right action to the left,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:351:where idempotence absorbs the repeated projector. This is the perfect
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:352:ancillary consistency used in item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:353:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:369:/-- The EPR quadratic forms of the Pauli line projectors on one half sum to
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:370:one. Formalization-only auxiliary for the ancillary overlaps in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:371:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:372:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-545`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:407:/-- The diagonal overlap of the two Pauli line measurements on an EPR pair is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:408:one. Thus the ancillary measurement contributes no consistency defect. This
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:409:is the perfect ancillary consistency in item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:410:paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:5:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:6:# Self-consistency of the expanded line measurements
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:7:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:8:This module proves item 1 of the expanded-line consistency lemma on the two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:9:opposite-placement bipartitions. The strategy line measurements are
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:10:self-consistent between the two players on average over the line-point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11:distribution, because a disagreement on a sampled line is rejected by the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12:corresponding self-loop of the Pauli basis test; the Pauli line projectors are
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:13:perfectly consistent on an EPR pair; and the data-processing inequality
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:14:transfers the product estimate to the addition postprocessing that defines the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:15:expanded line measurement.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:16:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:17:The module also records that the error parameter of a projective setting is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:18:nonnegative, which is not assumed by the structure and is needed by the other
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:19:two items as well.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:20:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:21:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:22:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:23:The declarations formalize `enu:qld-comm-line-self-cons`, item 1 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:24:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, whose paper source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:25:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:26:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:37:/-! ## Self-consistency of the unexpanded line measurements -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:39:/-- Mismatch mass of the two folded line answers at one sampled line.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:40:Formalization-only auxiliary for the strategy input to item 1 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:41:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:42:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:52:/-- Full line-measurement inconsistency is the probability that the two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:53:folded line answers differ. This is the line self-loop specialization used in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:54:item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:55:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:97:/-- The axis component of the line-point sampler is the axis-line self-loop
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:98:branch of the Pauli basis test. Formalization-only auxiliary for item 1 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:99:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:100:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:123:/-- The diagonal component of the line-point sampler is the diagonal-line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:124:self-loop branch of the Pauli basis test. Formalization-only auxiliary for
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:125:item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:126:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:149:/-- The two strategy line measurements are self-consistent on average over
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:150:the line-point distribution, with the rejection bound of the two line

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:3:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:4:# Square-root error bounds for placed measurement families
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:5:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:6:The consistency conclusions of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons` are stated with the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:7:common error `deltaLine ε = √ε`, while the individual estimates of the proof
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:8:are linear in `ε` or already of square-root form. This module records the two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:9:elementary facts that convert those estimates into the common form: the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:10:state-dependent distance between two placed complete measurements never
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:11:exceeds `4`, and a quantity bounded by both `a * ε` and `4` is bounded by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:12:`(a + 4) * √ε`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:13:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:14:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:15:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:16:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:17:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-545`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:18:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:29:/-- The adjoint squares of a complete measurement sum to at most the identity.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:30:This is the existing public measurement bound, used here for the uniform
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:31:distance estimate. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:37:/-- A left-placed complete measurement is square-summable on the product
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:38:space, by the public measurement bound applied to its tensor placement. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:47:/-- A right-placed complete measurement is square-summable on the product
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:48:space, by the public measurement bound applied to its tensor placement. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:57:/-- The squared distance between two square-summable operator families is at
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:58:most four on a unit vector. Formalization-only auxiliary bounding the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:59:state-dependent distance of `def:povm-distance` trivially. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:93:/-- The state-dependent distance between two complete measurements placed on
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:94:opposite tensor factors is at most four. Formalization-only auxiliary: this is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:95:the trivial bound used to pass from a linear error to the common square-root
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:96:error of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:97:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-545`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:121:/-- A nonnegative quantity bounded by a linear error `a * ε` with `1 ≤ a` and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:122:by the trivial bound `4` is bounded by `(a + 4) * √ε`: for `ε ≤ 1` the linear
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:123:bound dominates, and for `ε ≥ 1` the trivial bound does. Formalization-only
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:124:auxiliary: this is the passage to the common square-root error of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:125:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean:126:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-545`. -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:3:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:4:# Bipartite estimates and transport for the expanded line measurements
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:5:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:6:This module collects the generic distance estimates used by items 2 and 3 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:7:the expanded-line consistency lemma, and the identities that transport the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:8:placed families of the six-register expanded state to the two opposite-
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:9:placement bipartitions. The generic estimates are: the distance between two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:10:oppositely placed complete measurements is at most twice the complement of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:11:their diagonal overlap (`fact:agreement`), and a projective family compared
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:12:with itself followed by an effect selected through a coarse-graining is at
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:13:most as far as the coarse-grained families are from each other
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:14:(`fact:add-a-proj2` for a projective refinement). The transport identities
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:15:are formalization-only auxiliaries: they carry a relation between placed
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:16:operators on the six-register expanded state to the product shape in which the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:17:generic estimates are stated, a step the source leaves implicit.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:18:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:19:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:20:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:21:Items 2 and 3 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:22:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:23:blueprint `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons` and `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2`, and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:24:the generic estimates `fact:agreement` and `fact:add-a-proj2` of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:25:`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:26:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:37:/-! ## Generic bipartite estimates -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:41:/-- A projective effect is absorbed by the postprocessed effect of the fiber
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:42:containing its own outcome. Formalization-only auxiliary for the projective
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:43:refinement of `fact:add-a-proj2` used by `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:51:/-- The distance between two oppositely placed complete measurements is at
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:52:most twice their inconsistency, expressed through the diagonal overlap. This
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:53:is `fact:agreement` combined with the overlap form of the consistency defect. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:75:/-- A left-placed projective family, compared with itself followed by a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:76:right-placed effect selected through a coarse-graining, is at most as far
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:77:from it as the coarse-grained families are from each other. This is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:78:projective refinement step (`fact:add-a-proj2`) used to derive item 2 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:79:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons` from item 3, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:80:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-539`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:115:/-- A right-placed projective family, compared with itself followed by a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:116:left-placed effect selected through a coarse-graining, is at most as far from
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:117:it as the coarse-grained families are from each other. This is the projective
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:118:refinement of `fact:add-a-proj2` on the reversed directed pair. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:163:/-! ## Transport between the six registers and the bipartitions -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:166:/-- On the `AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition, an `AA'` placement followed by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:167:the product with a `BA''` placement acts on the expanded state as the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:168:corresponding left and right tensor placements. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:187:/-- The same transport with the roles of the two placements exchanged, so
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:188:that the `BA''` placement carries the left factor of the difference. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:208:/-- On the `AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition, the overlap of left and right
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:209:tensor placements is the overlap of the `AA'` and `BA''` placements. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:225:/-- On the `AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition, an `AB''` placement followed by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:226:the product with a `BB'` placement acts on the expanded state as the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:227:corresponding left and right tensor placements. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:246:/-- The same transport on the `AB'' | BB'` bipartition with the roles of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:247:two placements exchanged, so that the `BB'` placement carries the left factor
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:248:of the difference. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:268:/-- On the `AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition, the overlap of left and right
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:269:tensor placements is the overlap of the `AB''` and `BB'` placements. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:3:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:4:# Consistency of expanded evaluation classes with expanded points
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:5:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:6:This module proves item 3 of the expanded-line consistency lemma on the four
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:7:directed opposite-placement pairs. On each bipartition the distance between
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:8:the evaluation classes of the expanded line measurement and the completed
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:9:expanded point measurement is at most twice their inconsistency, which by the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:10:overlap identity equals the inconsistency of the strategy's evaluation classes
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:11:with its completed point measurement. The trivial bound `4` on the same
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:12:distance supplies the large-`ε` case of the common square-root error.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:13:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:14:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:15:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:16:Item 3 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:17:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:540-545`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:18:blueprint `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:19:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:34:/-! ## Overlaps of the evaluation classes -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:36:/-- Summed over outcomes, the overlap of Alice's expanded evaluation classes
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:37:with Bob's completed expanded point measurement on the expanded state equals
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:38:the corresponding overlap of the strategy's own evaluation classes with its
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:39:completed point measurement on the strategy state. The ancillary Pauli
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:40:projectors cancel because they agree exactly on the EPR pairs. This is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:41:identity behind `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:42:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:540-545`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:77:/-- The identity of `sum_stateQForm_evalClass_AA'_BA''_eq` with the two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/EvalClassConsistency.lean:78:placements exchanged, so that the evaluation classes are carried by the `BA''`

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:4:# Evaluation of line polynomials at a sampled point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:5:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:6:This module records the elementary calculus of the partial evaluation
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:7:`evalOpt` of a coefficient-list line polynomial at a point: the evaluation of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:8:a sum is the sum of the evaluations whenever both summands evaluate, a summand
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9:of an evaluating sum evaluates whenever the other summand does, the value is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:10:unique, and nothing evaluates at a point off the line. These facts underlie
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:11:the manipulation of the evaluation classes in items 2 and 3 of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:12:expanded-line consistency lemma.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:13:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:14:Every declaration below is a formalization-only auxiliary: the source uses
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:15:these facts about evaluation without stating them.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:16:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:17:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:18:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:19:The evaluation classes `[eval_u(·) = a]` are `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:20:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-58`. They are
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:21:manipulated in `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons` and `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:22:paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:23:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:31:/-- Coefficient-list evaluation is additive in the coefficient list. This
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:32:is the additivity behind the convolution of `def:expanded-line-measurement`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:40:/-- A line polynomial has at most one value at a point of the line: if it
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:41:evaluates both to `a` and to `b`, then `a = b`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:48:/-- The sum of two evaluating line polynomials evaluates to the sum of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:49:their values. This is why the convolution outcome `f = f' + f''` evaluates
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:50:whenever both convolution factors do. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:57:/-- If a sum and its second summand evaluate, the first summand evaluates to
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:58:the difference of their values. This is the converse direction used to identify
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:59:the convolution fibers of an evaluation class. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:69:/-- The partial evaluation returns `some a` exactly when the polynomial
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:70:evaluates to `a`. This is the characterization that makes `evalOpt` the total
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:71:form of the evaluation classes of `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:86:/-- The partial evaluation returns `none` exactly when no value is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:87:determined. This is the outcome that completes the evaluation classes to a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:88:measurement, written `[eval_u(·) = ⊥]` in `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:95:/-- The partial evaluation of a sum of two evaluating line polynomials is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:96:the sum of their values. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:105:/-- If a sum and its second summand evaluate, so does the first summand,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:106:with the difference of the two values. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:115:/-- A point at which some line polynomial evaluates lies on the line. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:121:/-- Off the line, no line polynomial evaluates, so every outcome falls in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:122:the `none` class. -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Expanded.lean:4:# Expanded line measurements
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Expanded.lean:5:

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Expanded.lean:7:line measurement with the Pauli-register line projectors, and records that the

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Expanded.lean:11:measurement is the addition postprocessing, and the evaluation-class and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Expanded.lean:12:point-effect families used by the consistency estimates.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Expanded.lean:17:source is

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Expanded.lean:69:/-- The line measurement of a projective strategy is again projective: folding

/-- A projective effect is absorbed by the postprocessed effect of the fiber
containing its own outcome. Formalization-only auxiliary for the projective
refinement of `fact:add-a-proj2` used by `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons`. -/
theorem effect_mul_postprocess_effect_self {α β ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
    [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ι)
    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (g : α → β) (a : α) :
    M.effect a * (M.postprocess g).effect (g a) = M.effect a := by
  simpa using SandwichProduct.effect_mul_postprocess_effect M hM g (g a) a

/-- The distance between two oppositely placed complete measurements is at
most twice their inconsistency, expressed through the diagonal overlap. This
is `fact:agreement` combined with the overlap form of the consistency defect. -/
theorem opFamilyDistSq_placed_le_two_mul_one_sub_overlap {X α ιA ιB : Type*}
    [Finite X] [Fintype α]
    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    (μ : Distribution X) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
    (A : X → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιA)
    (B : X → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιB)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) :
    opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).effect a) 1)
        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).effect a)) ψ ≤
      2 * (1 - avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a,
        stateQForm ψ (heteroKron ((A x).effect a) 1 *
          heteroKron 1 ((B x).effect a)))) := by
  classical
  letI : Fintype X := Fintype.ofFinite X
  refine (WinImplications.opFamilyDistSq_placed_le_two_mul_consistencyDefect
    μ A B ψ).trans (le_of_eq ?_)
  congr 1
  exact consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap μ
    (fun x => leftPlacedMeasurement (A x))
    (fun x => rightPlacedMeasurement (B x)) ψ hμ hψ

/-- A left-placed projective family, compared with itself followed by a
right-placed effect selected through a coarse-graining, is at most as far
from it as the coarse-grained families are from each other. This is the
projective refinement step (`fact:add-a-proj2`) used to derive item 2 of
`lem:qld-comm-line-cons` from item 3, paper

theorem opFamilyDistSq_left_refine_le {X α β ιA ιB : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    (μ : Distribution X) (M : X → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιA)
    (hM : ∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M x))
    (ev : X → α → β) (B : X → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement β ιB)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
    opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => heteroKron ((M x).effect a) 1)
        (fun x a => heteroKron ((M x).effect a) 1 *
          heteroKron 1 ((B x).effect (ev x a))) ψ ≤
      opFamilyDistSq μ

        (fun x b => heteroKron 1 ((B x).effect b)) ψ := by
  unfold opFamilyDistSq
  apply avgOver_mono
  intro x
  have hrw : ∀ a : α,
